evidence: node_modules/react-chatbot-kit (v2.2.2) package.json: main=build/index.js, no type/module/exports fields, so CommonJS. build/index.js is a webpack bundle using require('react') and ending in `module.exports=t`. Exports object t gets __esModule=true and getters via e.d(t,{Chatbot:()=>B,...,default:()=>H}) with H=B (Chatbot). So under webpack/Babel interop the default import resolves to exports.default = Chatbot; under Node ESM (no __esModule interop) the default import is the whole module.exports, with Chatbot as a property. Named exports are defined via Object.defineProperty getters and module.exports=t is a non-literal assignment, with no static `exports.Chatbot =`, so Node's cjs-module-lexer cannot detect `{ Chatbot }`, and a named import fails. The Vite case is the same non-interop shape the code handles with the `.Chatbot ?? chatbotKit` unwrap at ChatWidget.tsx:56. The comment matches the dependency.

ChatWidget.tsx:56 unwraps the default import. react-chatbot-kit 2.2.2 (package.json main build/index.js) build ends with module.exports=t where t has __esModule and exports Chatbot:()=>B and default:()=>H, with H=B (same function; build/index.js final segment 'H=B,module.exports=t'). Case 1 (Babel/webpack interop gives t.default): the import is the function B; no 'Chatbot' static is assigned to B (only grep hits for .Chatbot are none in build; src/index.ts exports Chatbot and default Chatbot), so (B).Chatbot is undefined and ?? falls back to B. Case 2 (Node ESM/Vite gives whole module.exports): .Chatbot is B. Both resolve to the same component.

SlashAutocomplete.tsx:29-33 setChatInputValue uses the native HTMLInputElement.prototype value setter and dispatches a bubbling 'input' Event, which triggers React's onChange. node_modules/react-chatbot-kit/src/components/Chat/Chat.tsx:66,307-310 renders the input with class react-chatbot-kit-chat-input, controlled by useState (value={input}, onChange sets state). ChatWidget.tsx:347-351: onTurnFailed reads the input synchronously and calls setChatInputValue (SlashAutocomplete.tsx:29-33, a synchronous native set plus input event) only when input exists and input.value is empty. Traced inputs: (1) typed then fully deleted: value empty, refill happens, and nothing typed is overwritten; (2) whitespace typed after submit: ' ' is truthy, so no refill; (3) pending prefill at lines 446-471: it applies immediately if the input exists, and the MutationObserver path only runs when no input exists. In that case onTurnFailed finds no input (or a prefilled, non-empty one) and does nothing, and the observer disconnects after applying once. No later overwrite of typed text; (4) kit leaving the input non-empty: guard skips the refill, which is the safe direction. Absolute claim holds: the only write path in onTurnFailed is guarded by the emptiness check at the moment of write.

The comment at src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx:237-240 exists as quoted. The code matches the first half: the effect at 241-249 subscribes keepInsideViewport to both window and visualViewport resize events, and the isOpen effect at 255-257 re-clamps on open. The second half, that emulated viewports never fire a second resize event, is a claim about browser and DevTools runtime behavior. Reading the repository cannot settle it, and I ran no browser or emulation. The comment at 251-253 says settling 'does not always fire a resize', which is consistent with it but not proof. keepInsideViewport reads window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight (230, via clampPosition), not visualViewport dimensions. So a visualViewport-only resize re-runs the check against window dimensions. Missing evidence: a DevTools device-emulation toggle run in a real browser, logging window and visualViewport resize events.

ChatWidget.tsx:255-257 runs keepInsideViewport when isOpen or keepInsideViewport (dep [dimensions], :229-235) changes, so every setDimensions during a resize re-runs it. keepInsideViewport calls setDimensions only if maxWidth differs from innerWidth, and setPosition(clampPosition(prev, dimensions)) returns prev when x,y are unchanged. clampPosition (:117-123) is idempotent, and the effect never changes width or height, so it cannot re-trigger itself: a second run is a no-op and there is no render loop. useResize (ResizeHandles.tsx:91-112) clamps width to [minWidth,maxWidth] with maxWidth=innerWidth and height to maxHeight. For left/top drags, computeResize (:71-78) keeps the opposite edge fixed (x = startLeft - growth, floored at 0). The right edge therefore stays at or below the viewport edge, and the viewport clamp is a no-op for the dragged edge. For pure top or left edge drags the effect never moves the window against the drag. Caveat: if the pointer leaves the window mid-drag, a mixed gesture such as top-right can have width exceed vw - x. useResize re-writes the stale startLeft x on each mousemove (:101), and the clamp then slides x back after each render. This is a transient per-mousemove correction with no loop, and it converges to an in-viewport state.

ChatWidget.tsx:558-579 sets inline minWidth/minHeight min(Npx,100%), maxWidth 100%, maxHeight min(Npx,100%) on the element with className radchat-container radchat-layout-floating (line 615-616). Inline styles beat non-!important CSS. In chat.css the only rules that match that element are .radchat-container (146-158: width/height 100%, no min/max) and :hover/[hidden] (display only). No .radchat-layout-floating rule exists. The sidebar/fullscreen/@media 520px rules with !important min/max (1020-1076, 1114-1118) target other layout classes, not floating. The only ancestor within the package is .radchat-widget (69-74), which sets z-index and font only, with no transform, filter or contain. Transform/filter rules in chat.css apply to buttons, icons and animations, not ancestors of the window. Absolute-claim input checked: a stylesheet !important min/max on .radchat-container; none exists. The comment's CSS statements (min wins over max, percentages resolve against the viewport for fixed positioning unless an ancestor has transform or filter) are correct CSS behavior. Host-page ancestors are outside the package and the comment already hedges them.

storage.ts:27-33 get returns window.localStorage.getItem(`${base}:${name}`) (the raw stored string, null if missing) and catches any throw, returning null. storage.ts:23 with prefix false returns NOOP_STORAGE whose get returns null and remove does nothing (lines 14-20). ChatWidget.tsx:413 reads saved via storage.get('conversation'); line 417 removes only when storage.get('conversation') === saved. saved is truthy (line 414), so a null from a throwing get or a noop storage never equals it and nothing is removed. The same storage object and key are used for both reads, so the value is unchanged unless something else wrote or removed it. Absolute-claim input traced: a localStorage access denial gives null on the second get, so no removal, and remove itself is try/catch guarded.

ChatController.ts:77-78 doc: 'A turn the user typed failed; `text` is what they typed.' Plain typed text is passed unchanged (handleUserInput line 245 -> performTurn 349 -> onTurnFailed line 411). Typed slash input is passed as text.trim() (line 242), so a command typed with leading/trailing whitespace reaches onTurnFailed trimmed, not verbatim. The callback is also skipped (line 397) when the turn is aborted, superseded by newConversation, or disposed; arguably those are cancellations, not failures. Staged attachments are taken (line 344) but do not change text. The only deviation is whitespace trimming of typed commands; no requirement from an unchanged file (e.g. a caller needing verbatim text) was found or checked beyond ChatWidget.tsx:347, which I did not read, so I cannot show either a broken requirement or full correctness.

Doc at src/types.ts:111-113. Code: ChatController.ts:387-395 silent = messages.length===0 && Array.isArray(blocks) && blocks.length===0, regardless of sources. (1) {blocks:[], sources:[{title:''}]}: sourcesToMarkdown (l.108-124) drops empty-title sources, answerToMessages returns [] (l.143), blocks.length===0 so turn is silent, though doc scopes silence to 'no sources'. src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx: appendBlocks (489-508) adds to appendedRef and, while the Chatbot for the latest reset key is not mounted (before first open, hasOpened gates render at 613), seeds initialMessages, so blocks appear on open. loadConversation with restore:true (370-406) keeps appendedRef.current in the seeded messages (392,396); a skipped restore (385-390) leaves the transcript untouched, so blocks stay. onNewConversation clears appendedRef (329) and resets to welcome. A History switch (restore not set) clears appendedRef (392), and the no-getConversation path clears it too (375). ChatWidget.tsx:489-508 appendBlocks makes one answerToMessages call (ChatController.ts:132-153: one message for all-plain-text or mixed blocks, none for blank/invalid), warns and ignores when empty, adds no user turn. Before first open (mountedResetKeyRef null != requestedResetKeyRef) it appends to initialMessages (l.504-505), which seeds the Chatbot on mount. src/chat/ChatController.ts:396-415: on sendMessage rejection the error is only console.error'd; displayed text is host.formatError(error), with fallback to defaultFormatError(error) if it throws (402-404). defaultFormatError (462-475) returns only one of four fixed strings: 401/403 sign-in, 429 rate limit, 'failed to fetch'/network message, or generic; the error message is only used for matching, never echoed. Traced: 'failed to fetch' -> fixed connection string; status 401 -> fixed sign-in string; formatError throwing -> default fixed string. onTurnFailed(text) at 411 receives `text`, the user's own input, not error data. Caveat: a host-supplied formatError could choose to show details, but that is the host's explicit override, which the README sentence frames as 'lets you change it'; the default behavior matches the claim.

src/mount.tsx:56 appendBlocks goes through withHandle (33-47), which pushes onto the shared `queued` array when ref.current is unset and flushes in push order (splice(0).forEach, line 44), so it is replayed in call order with open(). In the flush, open() calls setOpen(true), which calls setHasOpened(true) (ChatWidget.tsx:167-177). These updates are batched and no re-render has happened, so hasOpenedRef.current (454-457) is still false when the next queued appendBlocks runs. appendBlocks then takes the else branch (465-466) and buffers into initialMessages via setInitialMessages. The same batched render sets hasOpened true and the new initialMessages. chatConfig is memoised on initialMessages (503-504), and the Chatbot mounts only when hasOpened is true (572). It therefore mounts seeded with the appended blocks, so they show. If the widget was already opened, hasOpenedRef is true and controller.addMessages is used directly. Not run at runtime. I did not read how the Chatbot kit consumes initialMessages at mount, so that step rests on the memoised config and the mount gating.
